findings.text: Between units add-stack-realm-reset and add-stack-seeding the engine database is left unseeded before the journeys run. add-stack-realm-reset states that after 20-reset.sh the engine database holds the schema and 'no tenant, user, route or run; "E2E tenant" comes back from the next owner job or U61b's seeding'. add-stack-seeding adds no seeding step between 20 and 50: the seed runs only through the control server's POST /reset, i.e. when a test requests fresh_state (its STACK-ONLY row relies on 'the first fresh_state reset answers 204'). No spec states that every pytest journey, or the first one collected, takes fresh_state. On the fake profile the stack seeds before the engine starts, so existing journeys need not reset first. A journey that signs in before any reset would meet an engine with no E2E tenant, no idp route, no group maps and no catalogue, and fail; that breaks the batch outcome 'every journey so far passes'. Either a step (or 20-reset/resetMain) must seed after the reset, or the specs must state and test that every stack journey resets first.

Between add-audit-sink, add-stack-realm-reset and add-stack-conformance: after 20-reset.sh no sink route exists until a seed, so Mintkey events from steps 30 and 40 are answered 401. add-audit-sink assumes (UNVERIFIED) that the emitters retry every non-final status with back-off up to 30 s, four at a time. add-stack-conformance's sink probe waits 30 s for new rows; a backlog of retried 401 events could delay its events past that window. Only the late tenant_mismatch case is named in its Risks; the head-of-line delay is not.

The spec fixes only the TypeScript return types of `readUsers` (`Record<string, OverlayUser>`) and `readClients`. It never gives the JSON layout on disk: whether it is keyed by username or an array, the field names, or how a client secret is encoded. A later unit that reads the file directly, for example the Python journeys inside the runner, has no fixed contract. The only hint is the scenario 'a users.json missing `groups`'.

The overlay requirement lists rules that have no problem text and no row in `test-plan-rows.md`: the proxy's read-only mount `../.stack-e2e/ca:/etc/ursitoare-test-ca:ro`, the fakes TCP healthcheck on 443, the fakes aliases being on `egress` only, the networks of `runner` (`front`, `app`, `mintkey`, `egress`), and the image `ursitoare/stack-runner:local` on `fakes` and `runner`. Rows O1–O13 and the 'Also' line cover only part of the rule set. So `overlayProblems` may leave these rules out without any test failing. An implementer who adds them has to invent the texts, and each added rule must still keep the `null`/`[]`/`"x"` inputs at exactly 22 texts and the config-shaped fixture at `[]`.

The step rows imply that a line gets at most one S18 text, chosen in an order the spec never states. T19 (`docker run … docker.sock …`) must answer only 'names the Docker socket', although it is also 'docker outside the inspect pipe' (T11). T9 and T21 must answer only 'names a compose project', although they also break the `$COMPOSE` subcommand rule (T12). The implementer has to reverse-engineer the order from the rows.

`init-secrets` and `prepare` run through `$RUNNER`, the runner image, with no user set. They write 0600 files that compose then bind-mounts as secrets into the engine (user `node`), Postgres and the Mintkey containers. Nothing states who owns those files or whether those users can read them. The UNVERIFIED list and the STACK-ONLY table do not mention this either.

findings.text: The proposal's 'What later units take (fixed here)' lists `.stack-e2e/users.json` and `.stack-e2e/clients.json` as state that U61d, U61b and U61c consume. The spec fixes only the TypeScript return types of `readUsers` (`Record<string, OverlayUser>`) and `readClients`. It never gives the JSON layout on disk: whether it is keyed by username or an array, the field names, or how a client secret is encoded. A later unit that reads the file directly, for example the Python journeys inside the runner, has no fixed contract. The only hint is the scenario 'a users.json missing `groups`'.

The overlay requirement lists rules that have no problem text and no row in `test-plan-rows.md`: the proxy's read-only mount `../.stack-e2e/ca:/etc/ursitoare-test-ca:ro`, the fakes TCP healthcheck on 443, the fakes aliases being on `egress` only, the networks of `runner` (`front`, `app`, `mintkey`, `egress`), and the image `ursitoare/stack-runner:local` on `fakes` and `runner`. Rows O1–O13 and the 'Also' line cover only part of the rule set. So `overlayProblems` may leave these rules out without any test failing. An implementer who adds them has to invent the texts, and each added rule must still keep the `null`/`[]`/`"x"` inputs at exactly 22 texts and the config-shaped fixture at `[]`.

The step rows imply that a line gets at most one S18 text, chosen in an order the spec never states. T19 (`docker run … docker.sock …`) must answer only 'names the Docker socket', although it is also 'docker outside the inspect pipe' (T11). T9 and T21 must answer only 'names a compose project', although they also break the `$COMPOSE` subcommand rule (T12). The implementer has to reverse-engineer the order from the rows.

`init-secrets` and `prepare` run through `$RUNNER`, the runner image, with no user set. They write 0600 files that compose then bind-mounts as secrets into the engine (user `node`), Postgres and the Mintkey containers. Nothing states who owns those files or whether those users can read them. The UNVERIFIED list and the STACK-ONLY table do not mention this either.

The spec does not say what `projectMain` does when a subcommand's options are missing or malformed (for example `state` without `--present`, or `prepare` without `--dir`). It also does not say what happens when two `stack-e2e.sh` runs on the shared Mac work on project `ursitoare-e2e` at the same time.

`proxySmoke` puts a credential with `putCredential`, whose `VaultPutInput` needs `authScheme: number`, `headerName` and `callerActorId`. The spec gives the header name but not the `authScheme` value for header injection or the `callerActorId`. The implementer has to work them out from the fake's `wire.ts`.
